answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can act, and the deposit is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Creating a thousand sock-puppets then costs a thousand deposits, so a Sybil swarm is no longer free. The registry stays crystal clear, anyone can audit who staked what, while old proven identities keep their relic of trust, and newcomers earn their place in the haven of verified agents only after time and good behavior.
